name: gather timber
source: declared: the world holds it; a gather is not a transformation
note: 3000 g is one armful; the rate is declared [D], because no source states what a game gather costs

name: riven haft
source: declared: the record's own worked chain (MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 ceramics/knapping)
note: riving, not sawing: splitting along the grain is what the stone age can do

name: gather stone
source: declared: the world holds it; a gather is not a transformation
note: 1000 g is one carried load

name: knap a core
source: declared: the record's own worked chain (MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 ceramics/knapping)
note: the 800/200 split is declared [D]: real knapping loses more, but a usable edge is what the process is for

name: gather plant fibre
source: declared: the world holds it; a gather is not a transformation
note: 100 g is a bundle of brush

name: forage
source: declared: the world holds it; a gather is not a transformation
note: 2000 g is a person's day of eating, picked in half an hour of game time

name: hunt a hide
source: declared: the world holds it; a gather is not a transformation
note: a hide is the skin of a hunted animal; the hunt itself is the gather

name: twist cord
source: declared: the record's own worked chain (MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 ceramics/knapping)
note: the first process in bound & composite: binding is what makes a composite tool possible before metal

name: assemble the hatchet
source: declared: the record's own worked chain (MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 ceramics/knapping)
note: the chain's end: a hatchet from natural materials, the tool that multiplies work

name: fire brick
source: declared: fired brick 900–1000 °C (real kiln practice); MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 heat/furnace — the harvest measures no brick temperature (its 930 °C sample is brass)
note: 900-1000 C is what fired brick is fired at [V]; heat_kind is material because the clay body must reach it

name: char timber
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 pyrolysis/charring; Immersive-Weathering charred wood
note: a quarter of the wood's mass is charcoal, the low end of the real 20-35 % range [D]; 400 C is where wood pyrolyses [V]

name: burn charcoal
source: declared: charcoal burns at 700–900 °C in air; MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 heat/steam names charcoal as the fuel the boilers burn, and no harvest row measures a burn
note: the warming fire: heat_kind is flame here, because what a person warms hands on is the flame

name: calcine limestone
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 heat/furnace (kiln pyrotechnology); limestone's note names the kiln
note: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2, the stoichiometry read from the molar masses (100 -> 56 + 44)

name: calcine gypsum
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 ceramics; gypsum's note names the calcination
note: gypsum loses three quarters of a water molecule per sulfate: 1000 g of the dihydrate gives 790 g of the hemihydrate

name: make mortar
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 construction/brickmaking
note: one part lime, three parts sand, enough water to make a paste; the mix is declared

name: make a crucible
source: declared: a clay-graphite crucible is the real vessel [V]; MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 ceramics (TFC knapping/moulds) is the nearest harvest row and states no crucible
note: clay-graphite, the vessel that survives a melt; 100 g of the charge leaves as smoke

name: raise steam
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 heat/steam generation (SteamPowered, Railcraft SteamBoiler)
note: a kilo of water is a kilo of steam: the volume changes, the mass does not

name: crush copper ore
source: harvest: _harvest/create-processes/out.crushing (copper_ore -> crushed_raw_copper); Railcraft rock crusher
note: Create's measured crushing keeps the ore and loses a tenth to fines

name: wash crushed copper
source: harvest: _harvest/create-processes/out.splashing (crushed_raw_copper -> 9 copper nuggets + clay)
note: water dressing: the gangue leaves as clay and sludge, the metal stays; the 500 g copper is the ore's own content

name: crush iron ore
source: harvest: _harvest/create-processes/out.crushing; IC2 macerator; Railcraft rock crusher
note: the same rule as the copper row, applied to the iron ore

name: smelt copper
source: harvest: _harvest/gt-conditions.tsv TEMP Copper 1358, read as kelvin (=1085 °C, copper's melting point; the harvest flags the unit [NS]); MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 heat/furnace
note: malachite is 57.5 % copper by its formula; 1085 C is copper's melting point [V]

name: smelt tin
source: harvest: _harvest/gt-conditions.tsv TEMP Tin 505 (kelvin; 232 °C melting point); the 1200 °C reduction temperature is declared [D]
note: cassiterite SnO2 is 78.8 % tin; 1200 C clears tin's 232 C melting point with the slag fluid

name: smelt zinc
source: harvest: _harvest/gt-conditions.tsv TEMP Zinc 693 (kelvin; 420 °C melting point); a retort must hold 1100 °C because zinc boils at 907 °C [V]
note: a sulfide ore needs roasting before reduction; the row states the reduction, and zinc's 670 g is ZnS's 67 %

name: smelt bismuth
source: harvest: _harvest/gt-conditions.tsv TEMP Bismuth 545 (kelvin; 272 °C melting point); the 1000 °C charge temperature is declared [D]
note: Bi2S3 is 81.3 % bismuth; 545 K is bismuth's melting point, and the slag must stay fluid above it

name: smelt nickel
source: harvest: _harvest/gt-conditions.tsv TEMP Nickel 1728 (kelvin; 1455 °C melting point); the 1500 °C charge temperature is declared [D]
note: garnierite is a hydrous silicate: 40 % nickel is the high end of the real range [D], the rest is slag

name: smelt tetrahedrite
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 heat/furnace firing; TFC ore roster
note: Cu12Sb4S13 carries both metals; the two outputs are its own copper and antimony

name: alloy bronze
source: harvest: _harvest/stage-a-passes.md §TFC alloy ranges (bronze 0.88–0.92 Cu + 0.08–0.12 Sn); MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 forming/casting
note: nine parts copper to one of tin, melted together: the bronze leaves the furnace as a melt, and the cast is what makes it a bar

name: alloy brass
source: harvest: _harvest/stage-a-passes.md §TFC alloy ranges (brass 0.88–0.92 Cu + 0.08–0.12 Zn); Create mixing copper + zinc -> brass_ingot
note: nine parts copper to one of zinc, inside TFC's measured range; Create's mixing recipe fixes the pair but no ratio

name: melt copper
source: harvest: _harvest/gt-conditions.tsv TEMP Copper 1358 (kelvin; 1085 °C melting point); MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 forming/casting (TFC casting 111, 100 mb + mould)
note: copper at its own melting point, held long enough to pour: the first state change the tree declares

name: melt tin
source: harvest: _harvest/gt-conditions.tsv TEMP Tin 505 (kelvin; 232 °C melting point)
note: tin melts in a ladle over a fire: 232 °C is the metal's own point, not a furnace's

name: melt zinc
source: harvest: _harvest/gt-conditions.tsv TEMP Zinc 693 (kelvin; 420 °C melting point)
note: zinc melts at 420 °C and boils at 907 °C, so the melt is short-lived and the retort is closed

name: cast bronze
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 forming/casting (TFC casting 111: 100 mb + ceramic mould -> head); the mould is a structure, not a consumed row
note: poured into a mould: the same bronze, but a mould is what makes it a part instead of a puddle

name: cast brass
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 forming/casting (TFC casting 111); the mould is the same ceramic tooling
note: brass pours cooler than bronze and fills a finer mould

name: smelt magnetite
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 heat/bloomery (TFC bloomery reduces ore with charcoal); the 1400 °C and the yields are declared [D]
note: Fe3O4 is 72.4 % iron; 700 g of the metal is the ore's own iron, the rest is slag and gas

name: smelt limonite
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 heat/bloomery (TFC bloomery reduces ore with charcoal); the 1400 °C and the yields are declared [D]
note: limonite is a hydrated oxide: its 55 % iron is the lower grade the hydrates carry

name: coke coal
source: harvest: _harvest/railcraft-values.tsv (coke_oven, 1800 ticks, 500 mb creosote); the mod's 500 mb is a fluid yield, not a mass ratio — 535 g of creosote would leave 465 g of coke — so the 85/15 coke-to-creosote split is declared [D] against real coking yields
note: Railcraft's coke oven: coal carbonised to coke with creosote as the second product, 1800 ticks

name: bloom iron
source: declared: bloomery reduction of ore concentrate; the harvest's bloomery row (charcoal ×2 + 100 mb cast iron → bloom, 14,400 t) is the cast-iron fining step, and its masses do not apply here
note: a bloomery never melts the iron: it reduces the ore to a spongy bloom the hammer consolidates

name: blast steel
source: harvest: _harvest/railcraft-values.tsv (blast_furnace iron_ingot -> steel_ingot, 1280 ticks, 1 slag); an ingot-for-ingot pair and a slag count fix no masses, so the 900 g of steel, the 300 g of slag and the 250 g of coke are declared [D]
note: Railcraft's blast furnace: iron plus slag, 1280 ticks; the carbon comes from the coke

name: cast iron
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 heat/blast conversion (Railcraft blast furnace iron -> steel, 1280 t); TFC cast iron; the carbon pick-up is declared [D]
note: iron held above 2 % carbon is fluid enough to pour: the cast iron the blast furnace gives

name: forge weld
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 forging/welding (TFC welding 87)
note: a flux weld: borax dissolves the scale so two billets become one; 20 g of it leaves as slag

name: anvil work
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 forging/anvil work (TFC anvil 281, welding 87)
note: TFC's ordered anvil steps: the shape is struck, and a twentieth of the steel leaves as scale

name: melt iron
source: harvest: _harvest/gt-conditions.tsv (iron's own melting point, 1538 °C [V]); MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 heat/blast conversion
note: the blast furnace's product leaves molten; 1538 °C is what keeps it liquid

name: crush rock
source: harvest: _harvest/create-processes/out.crushing; _harvest/railcraft-values.tsv (rock_crusher stone -> cobblestone)
note: a jaw crusher takes a stone to gravel and fines, the same rule Create's crushing row states

name: sift gravel
source: harvest: _harvest/stage-a-passes.md §createsifter (153 recipe JSONs; gravel -> crushed ore, pebbles, nuggets)
note: screening splits the coarse from the sand; the shaker's own measured example is a gravel

name: mill grain
source: harvest: _harvest/create-processes/out.milling (wheat -> flour); TFC quern 89
note: a quern is two stones: three quarters of the grain is flour, the husk is bran

name: press a sheet
source: harvest: _harvest/create-processes/out.pressing (sheets); IC2 metal former rolling
note: Create's press: an ingot becomes a plate, and scale leaves the surface

name: draw wire
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 forming/wire drawing (CDG wire_cutting, GT wiremill, IC2 extruding)
note: copper is drawn through a die: five percent is lost to the die and the anneal

name: roll a rail
source: harvest: _harvest/railcraft-values.tsv (rolling_machine, steel_ingot:6 -> rail:16); six-to-sixteen counts toy items, so the 950 g rail and its 5 % scale are declared [D]
note: Railcraft's rolling machine: six steel ingots to sixteen rail sections

name: dress stone
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 masonry/stone dressing (TFC chisel 513, Create cutting)
note: TFC's chisel: a squared block costs a tenth of the stone as chippings

name: weave cloth
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 textiles/sewing (TFC loom 5, sewing 25)
note: TFC's loom: fibre becomes cloth, the short fibres leave as dust

name: impregnate timber
source: declared: creosote timber preservation is real practice [V]; _harvest/railcraft-values.tsv measures creosote as the coke oven's product (500 mb), and §8.1 woodworking measures oil impregnation (Forestry)
note: creosote and pressed oil under pressure: the sleeper that does not rot

name: plant grain
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 agriculture/planting (MFR Planter/Harvester, TFC farming) and agriculture/composting; the yield is declared [D]
note: a crop's mass is mostly air and water, and the compost is what lets it take them up: 100 g seed, 1000 g water, 500 g compost and 1900 g carbon dioxide give 3500 g of grain

name: press seed oil
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 separation/extraction (Forestry squeezer: 250 mb seed oil -> impregnated casing); the pressing yield is declared [D]
note: mechanical extraction: the oil leaves the seed under pressure, and the cake is what remains

name: extract the press cake
source: harvest: _harvest/gt-material-ids.txt (ethanol) and _harvest/gt-conditions.tsv (HAZARD Ethanol) name the solvent, and _harvest/forestry still measures the process that makes it (10 mb biomass -> 3 mb bio-ethanol); no artifact measures a solvent extraction, so the wash ratio, the 92 % oil recovery and the 99.5 % solvent recovery are declared [D]
note: solvent extraction: ethanol at its own boiling point dissolves the oil a press cannot reach, and is boiled back off the meal — the second half of §8.1's extraction rule, on a solvent the harvest names and the tree already makes

name: raise livestock
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 agriculture/husbandry (MFR Rancher/Breeder/Slaughterhouse/Grinder/MeatPacker, 43 machines; MFR meat fluid 2000 kg/m3; Ecologics fauna); the feed-to-meat ratio and the breath are declared [D]
note: the animal is the process: forage and water become meat, hide, wet manure and breath; 550 g leaves as carbon dioxide, because an animal that respires nothing is not an animal. The ratio is a game rate, not a carcass measurement, and the manure is mostly water the animal drank

name: compost biomass
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 agriculture/composting (MFR Composter; Forestry bog earth/peat); the 30-day turn cycle, the 1900 g yield and the 600 g of vented gas are declared [D]
note: the heap self-heats to 55-65 C [V]; 30 days and four turns is the declared cycle, and the 600 g that leaves as carbon dioxide is the dry matter the heap burns

name: distil crude oil
source: harvest: _harvest/tekkit-fluids.tsv (BuildCraft oil 900, residue 1200, tar); MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 separation/distillation (CDG splits) — the diesel/gasoline split itself is declared [D]
note: fractional distillation separates by boiling range: the middle fraction is diesel, the light one gasoline, the residue tar

name: ferment biomass
source: harvest: _harvest/forestry still (10 mb biomass -> 3 mb bio-ethanol); MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 separation/fermentation; the still's ratio is by volume, so the 300 g of ethanol per kilogram and the sludge are declared [D]
note: Forestry's measured 10-to-3 still ratio; the carbon dioxide is the fermentation's gas

name: tan hides
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 chemistry/tanning (TFC scraping 7 + barrel)
note: TFC's barrel: bark liquor tans the hide, and the wet sludge is what leaves the vat

name: grind cinnabar
source: declared: cinnabar → vermilion is the historical pigment; MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 chemistry/dyeing (GT dye set) is the nearest harvest row
note: the red pigment is ground, not made: a tenth of the mineral leaves as dust

name: weather copper
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 weathering/oxidation (Immersive-Weathering exposed->oxidized; Create deploying 167)
note: the patina's oxygen comes from the air, which this table has no row for: the water is the visible half

name: frost shatter stone
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 weathering/frost (Immersive-Weathering frost, frosty glass)
note: water in the cracks freezes, expands and splits the rock: the freeze-thaw rule, with the water's 20 g in the mass

name: mix black powder
source: declared: 75/15/10 saltpeter/charcoal/sulfur is the real composition [V]; the harvest is silent (GT lists saltpeter and gunpowder as material ids only, no process)
note: the historic 75/10/15: saltpeter, sulfur, charcoal, and nothing else

name: make glass
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 glass/glassworking (TFC glassworking 60, molten glass 2400 density); Forestry liquid glass
note: forest glass: sand, the potash in wood ash, and lime; 1450 C is the furnace's working temperature

name: blow glass
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 glass/glassworking (TFC glassworking 60)
note: a blown vessel: a tenth of the gather is lost to the pipe and the anneal

name: refine potash
source: declared: potash from wood ash is real chemistry; MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 agriculture/composting (MFR Composter) is the nearest harvest row, and sylvite is an ore row, not a process
note: sylvite is the potassium salt; refining it leaves the halite it came with and a little sludge

name: bake bread
source: harvest: _harvest/create-processes/out.smoking, out.campfire_cooking; MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 agriculture
note: the loaf is flour and water; the tenth that leaves is the steam of the bake

name: harvest biomass
source: declared: the world holds it; a gather is not a transformation
note: green matter cut from the world: the fermenter's feed, and a fuel

name: tap a tree
source: declared: the world holds it; a gather is not a transformation
note: Rubberworks' sapping: 40 mb of resin a species, gathered rather than made

name: curdle rubber
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 arboriculture/sapping (Rubberworks 500 mb resin -> 2 rubber); a fluid-to-item pair fixes no masses, so the 80/20 rubber-to-sludge split is declared [D]
note: Rubberworks' measured ratio: the latex coagulates to rubber and a fifth leaves as sludge

name: assemble a mechanism
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 assembly/mechanical assembly (Create mechanical_crafting, sequenced_assembly)
note: Create's assembly: plates, wire, a bronze bearing and a cast part become one working thing

name: melt glass
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 glass/glassworking (TFC glassworking 60; molten glass density 2400)
note: a gather is glass above 1100 °C: molten glass is what the pipe actually holds

name: leach copper ore
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 sizing/washing (IC2 ore washer: 1000 mb water per crushed ore) and separation/extraction; the liquor's carry is declared [D]
note: water and sulfur make the acid that carries the copper: the liquor is the ore's copper in solution, the residue is its gangue

name: centrifuge the leach
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 separation/centrifugation (GT centrifuge, IC2 thermal_centrifuge); the fines are declared [D]
note: the vat cannot settle every fine; a centrifuge throws them out without cooling the solution

name: dye cloth
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 chemistry/soaking-brining-dyeing (TFC barrel 331; GT dye set; MFR ceramic dye 16); _harvest/stage-a-passes.md §BluePower measures indigo dye from a real plant
note: ash lye is the mordant, vermilion the pigment: the cloth keeps the colour it is boiled in

name: refine silicon
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 electronics/silicon refining (RS2 quartz -> silicon 200 t; BluePower boule 8 coal + 8 sand)
note: SiO2 + 2C -> Si + 2CO: 1000 g of quartz gives 467 g of silicon and 933 g of off-gas

name: saw a wafer
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 electronics/wafer doping (BluePower dopes wafers; PR rough_silicon_wafer)
note: the ingot is sawed, not split: a twentieth of the silicon is kerf

name: make a circuit
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 electronics/circuit making (Calculator chambers, RS2 processors)
note: a wafer, its copper traces and an insulating glass: the three parts a working circuit is

name: electrowin copper
source: harvest: MODS-MATERIALS §8.1 separation/electrolysis (GT electrolyzer); the cell's yield is declared [D] against real electrowinning
note: current through the liquor plates the copper back out; the spent liquor returns to the leach
